answer: Stake-gated reputation blocks Sybils. Each identity locks a refundable bond, logged as a violet registry entry, and per-epoch earnings are capped by a reputation meter that rises only when peers verify real work. A farm pays full bond per key while each starts at zero standing, so marginal yield stays near zero until actual verification labor is absorbed. Detected clusters freeze as one terrace-shaped pool of bonds, and slashing a false claim costs more than the payout. So attackers pay near honest cost, ending the Sybil discount; opal-grade evidence makes forged proofs hard to launder.
